variants.title: Give each part its job
variants.context: etcd is a strongly consistent, replicated key-value store for small pieces of coordination state. Distributed systems use it for configuration, service registration, leader election, ownership, and other decisions where two clients must not observe conflicting committed answers.
variants.prompt: From the lesson section “Use revisions as the coordination clock”: match each part to its responsibility.

pairs.label: Range
pairs.detail: Read one key or a byte range at the current or an available historical revision.
pairs.explanation: Read one key or a byte range at the current or an available historical revision. Use the response header revision as a cache or multi-request snapshot boundary.

pairs.label: Transaction
pairs.detail: Evaluate version, revision, lease, or value comparisons and atomically run the success or failure branch.
pairs.explanation: Evaluate version, revision, lease, or value comparisons and atomically run the success or failure branch. All writes in one transaction share one revision.

pairs.label: Watch
pairs.detail: Stream events from a chosen revision.
pairs.explanation: Stream events from a chosen revision. Reconnect from the last processed revision and relist when required history has already been compacted.

pairs.label: Lease
pairs.detail: Attach keys to a server-managed TTL.
pairs.explanation: Attach keys to a server-managed TTL. Expiry or revoke deletes every attached key and produces delete events, but external side effects still need fencing or idempotency.

variants.hint: Give each part the one job only it can do, then rule out the rest. The core invariant is one durable order of committed key-value operations while a voting majority can communicate.
variants.explanation: Each part has a distinct responsibility. Range: Read one key or a byte range at the current or an available historical revision. Transaction: Evaluate version, revision, lease, or value comparisons and atomically run the success or failure branch. Watch: Stream events from a chosen revision. Lease: Attach keys to a server-managed TTL.

variants.title: Give each part its job
variants.context: etcd is a strongly consistent, replicated key-value store for small pieces of coordination state. Distributed systems use it for configuration, service registration, leader election, ownership, and other decisions where two clients must not observe conflicting committed answers.
variants.prompt: From the lesson section “Distinguish compaction from defragmentation”: match each part to its responsibility.

pairs.label: Delete
pairs.explanation: Deletes current application data. Old MVCC revisions can remain until compaction, so a delete alone does not necessarily reduce backend history or filesystem size.

pairs.label: Compact
pairs.detail: Marks historical revisions before a boundary unavailable and lets the backend reuse their pages.
pairs.explanation: Marks historical revisions before a boundary unavailable and lets the backend reuse their pages. Watchers behind that boundary must relist.

pairs.label: Defragment
pairs.detail: Rebuilds one member's backend to release reusable pages to the filesystem.
pairs.explanation: Rebuilds one member's backend to release reusable pages to the filesystem. Defragmenting a live member blocks its reads and writes, so schedule members separately.

variants.hint: Give each part the one job only it can do, then rule out the rest. The core invariant is one durable order of committed key-value operations while a voting majority can communicate.
variants.explanation: Each part has a distinct responsibility. Delete: Deletes current application data. Compact: Marks historical revisions before a boundary unavailable and lets the backend reuse their pages. Defragment: Rebuilds one member's backend to release reusable pages to the filesystem.

variants.prompt: From the lesson section “Reconfigure membership one member at a time”: match each part to its responsibility.

pairs.label: Prove the current majority
pairs.detail: Record member IDs, leader, Raft term and index, endpoint health, alarms, database size, peer latency, snapshot integrity, and the tested rollback path.
pairs.explanation: Record member IDs, leader, Raft term and index, endpoint health, alarms, database size, peer latency, snapshot integrity, and the tested rollback path.

pairs.label: Add a learner or replace one voter
pairs.detail: For expansion, add a non-voting learner when supported.
pairs.explanation: For expansion, add a non-voting learner when supported. For replacement, preserve the remaining majority and use exact peer URLs, TLS identity, and cluster state.

pairs.label: Wait for catch-up
pairs.detail: Verify applied index, data integrity, peer traffic, and stable leader behavior.
pairs.explanation: Verify applied index, data integrity, peer traffic, and stable leader behavior. A started process is not proof that the member is ready to vote.

pairs.label: Promote or finish removal
pairs.detail: Promote the learner or complete the one-member replacement only after the release gate passes.
pairs.explanation: Promote the learner or complete the one-member replacement only after the release gate passes. Then refresh the snapshot and membership inventory.

Promote or finish removal: Promote the learner or complete the one-member replacement only after the release gate passes.

variants.prompt: A three-voter etcd cluster loses one voting member. How many live voters remain, and can writes still commit?
options: Two remain; writes can commit because two is the majority
Two remain; writes stop because all three voters are required
One remains; writes can commit through the leader alone
One remains; serializable reads require a new election
variants.explanation: A three-voter cluster has a quorum of two. One voter can be unavailable while the remaining two still elect a leader and commit writes.

A three-voter cluster has a quorum of two. One voter can be unavailable while the remaining two still elect a leader and commit writes.

A three-voter cluster has a quorum of two. One voter can be unavailable while the remaining two still elect a leader and commit writes.
